soffit_surface_input_group.description: Rate per SF applies to net soffit field area from PaintScope. Engine divides SF by rate to calculate hours. ALL base rates in this spec already include overhead work penalty (~25-35% reduction from vertical baselines). Do NOT apply FAC_SFIT_OVERHEAD as a separate stacking modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Ground Protection Below Soffit
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy plastic sheeting and tarps over landscape below soffit work zone. ~18 sec per SF. Soffit protection covers larger drip fallout zone than siding (gravity pulls all drips straight down from overhead). SF-based per resolution (area of landscape to cover). Slower than siding perimeter-based protection because full area coverage required for overhead work.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Coverage adequate below working area. Minor gaps acceptable if brush/roll method.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of landscape within drip fallout zone. Secured against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage with no gaps. Secured at all edges.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection Below Soffit
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on flat walkway and patio surfaces below soffit. ~14 sec per SF. Ground-level task — no overhead penalty. Same rate as siding sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Key areas covered below working zone.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of walkways and patios within drip zone.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage taped at edges. Non-slip canvas on crew traffic areas.

task_production_rates.name: Soffit-Mounted Light Fixture Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Bag and tape soffit-mounted fixtures overhead — recessed lights, porch fixtures, vent covers. ~6 min per fixture. Slower than siding fixture masking (15 EA/hr) because overhead access adds time for taping and bagging above head.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. All fixtures fully masked. Recessed light rings taped.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage with clean tape lines. Cover plates removed where accessible.

task_production_rates.name: Fascia Junction Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply tape and 12-inch masking film along fascia-soffit junction when fascia is already finished. Rate expressed per SF of soffit area (proxy for perimeter length). ~7 sec per SF equivalent. Overhead taping is slower than vertical. Only needed when fascia is already painted — skipped in top-down NC sequence.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Tape at fascia junction. Film covers fascia face.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Clean tape line at junction. Film secured against drips.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Precision tape line. Film fully covers fascia face. No gaps.

task_production_rates.name: Brush/Roll Equipment Setup for Overhead Work
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Stage brushes, rollers, trays, extension poles (4-8 ft) for overhead application, and set up ladders/scaffold per access_type. ~25 min per elevation. Slightly longer than siding setup (20 min) due to extension pole assembly and overhead tool staging.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Equipment staged and functional. Extension pole assembled.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Fresh roller covers. Brushes in good condition. Extension pole tested.
defect_tolerance.QT4: New roller covers. Premium brushes. Extension pole secure. Materials pre-mixed.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Equipment Setup for Overhead Work (Non-Vented Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Configure airless sprayer with 413-515 tip for overhead application, test spray pattern overhead, run lines, stage materials. Lower pressure settings required for overhead overspray control. ~50 min per elevation. Longer than siding spray setup (45 min) due to overhead pressure calibration and expanded ground protection verification. NON-VENTED SOFFIT ONLY.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Equipment functional. Tip pattern acceptable overhead.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern verified overhead on cardboard. Correct tip for substrate.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment calibrated for overhead. Test pattern at correct distance. Backup tips staged. Pressure verified for minimal overspray.

task_production_rates.name: Low-Pressure Wash Soffit Surface
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Garden hose + soft bristle brush overhead from ladder/scaffold. ~10 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 500-600 SF/hr, overhead: 300-400 SF/hr). Washing overhead is slower — must manage water runoff, work at awkward angle, and move ladder frequently. HIGH-PRESSURE POWER WASHING PROHIBITED on soffit.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All construction dust, dirt, cobwebs removed. Surface clean to touch. Allow 24 hr dry.
defect_tolerance.QT4: TSP/mildewcide solution wash. Pristine surface. Allow 24-48 hr dry time.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Wood Soffit for Adhesion
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 80-120 grit sand for adhesion profile on bare wood soffit overhead. ~24 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 200-250 SF/hr, overhead: 120-180 SF/hr). Hand blocks for T&G grooves, orbital sander for flat panels. Overhead sanding is fatiguing — dust falls into eyes. PPE mandatory.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full surface sand. T&G grooves hand-sanded.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full surface sand with uniform scratch pattern. Inspect all T&G grooves.

task_production_rates.name: Scuff Sand Fiber Cement Soffit
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 150 grit light scuff sand factory-primed HardieSoffit panels overhead. ~20 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 200-250 SF/hr, overhead: 140-200 SF/hr). Lighter grit and smoother surface than bare wood — slightly faster. Required on factory-primed surfaces for adhesion tooth.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Light scuff pattern visible. Not removing material — creating tooth.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform scratch pattern across full surface overhead. No missed areas.

task_production_rates.name: Scuff Sand Vinyl Soffit
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 220 grit scuff sand glossy vinyl soffit panels overhead for bonding primer adhesion. ~20 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 200-250 SF/hr, overhead: 140-200 SF/hr). Same rate as FC scuff sand — similar light pressure required. Non-negotiable step for vinyl — without it, coating peels in sheets.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Full surface scuff. No gloss remaining.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full surface scuff sand. Uniform dull finish.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full surface scuff. Uniform scratch pattern. No missed areas.

task_production_rates.name: End-Seal Fiber Cement Cut Edges
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush end-cut sealer on each field-cut edge of HardieSoffit panels overhead. ~72 sec per cut edge. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical/ground baseline: 60-80 EA/hr, overhead: 40-60 EA/hr). Includes butt joints, miters, and field cuts. Overhead access makes this slower — must reach panel edges from ladder while managing sealer drips.
task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Count of soffit panel cut edges. Not captured by PaintScope — estimator enters count based on soffit panel layout. Typical: 2-4 cuts per panel for butt joints and field cuts.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All cut edges sealed with full coverage. No bare cellulose visible.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All cut edges sealed. Inspect for completeness. Critical for FM-006 prevention.

task_production_rates.name: Spot-Prime Tannin Knots on Wood Soffit
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush alkyd/shellac stain blocker onto individual knots overhead. ~3 min per knot. Overhead brush detail work — must manage drips of fast-drying alkyd/shellac product. Allow flash-off before full prime coat.
task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Count of visible tannin knots on bare cedar/redwood/fir soffit boards. Estimator enters count based on visual inspection. Typical: 1-3 knots per 8 ft board on T&G cedar.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All visible knots and sap streaks spot-primed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All knots spot-primed. Inspect under bright light for missed tannin sources.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Soffit Panel Joints and Junctions
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply and tool exterior paintable caulk overhead at soffit panel joints and soffit-to-fascia/frieze junctions. ~65 sec per LF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 75-100 LF/hr, overhead: 45-70 LF/hr). Gravity pulls caulk from the bead — requires careful application technique overhead. Caulk AFTER primer coat.
task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Linear feet of soffit panel joints and soffit-to-trim junctions requiring caulk. Includes panel butt joints, fascia junctions, frieze junctions. Does NOT include vent perforations.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All panel joints and fascia/frieze junctions caulked. Smooth tool.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead. Precision tool smooth overhead.

task_production_rates.name: Prep Dust Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth dust removal from soffit surface overhead after sanding. ~9 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 500-600 SF/hr, overhead: 300-500 SF/hr). Much dust falls away from overhead surface due to gravity — but residual particles must still be removed for adhesion.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All sanding dust removed. Surface ready for primer.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Pristine surface. No visible dust. Tack cloth verification pass.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Brush/Roll Overhead (Wood/FC)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush for fascia/frieze junctions and T&G grooves, roller with extension pole for open field overhead. ~30 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 150-200 SF/hr, overhead: 100-150 SF/hr). Acrylic primer (SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_ACRYLIC) for bare wood and factory-primed FC. Default method for all vented soffits.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Work primer into T&G grooves. Maintain wet edge overhead.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage with consistent roller texture. No lap marks. All grooves fully coated.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Spray Overhead (Wood/FC, Non-Vented Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray primer on soffit overhead. ~14 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 300-450 SF/hr, overhead: 200-300 SF/hr). NON-VENTED SOFFIT ONLY. Lower pressure settings for overhead overspray control. Acrylic primer for wood/factory-primed FC.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage overhead. No holidays or thin spots.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build overhead. Full coverage.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Inspect under raking light at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Bonding Primer Brush/Roll Overhead (Vinyl)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply bonding primer (SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_BONDING) by brush/roller with extension pole on vinyl soffit overhead. ~33 sec per SF. Slightly slower than acrylic primer on wood/FC because bonding primer is tackier and harder to maintain wet edge. Overhead penalty baked in. Recoat within 1 week.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays on non-porous surface.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Full adhesion bond. Maintain wet edge overhead.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage. Consistent film build. No lap marks.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Bonding Primer Spray Overhead (Vinyl, Non-Vented Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply bonding primer by airless spray on non-vented vinyl soffit overhead. ~16 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in. NON-VENTED ONLY. Bonding primer spray is slightly slower than acrylic primer spray due to product viscosity.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. Full coverage.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage. Inspect under raking light.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Alkali-Resistant Brush/Roll Overhead (Bare FC)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply alkali-resistant primer (SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_ALKALI) by brush/roller on bare/damaged fiber cement soffit overhead. ~36 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in. Slower than acrylic primer because bare FC is more porous — absorbs primer heavily, requiring more material and slower application to maintain coverage.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Full primer penetration. Maintain wet edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage. Consistent film build on porous substrate.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Alkali-Resistant Spray Overhead (Bare FC, Non-Vented Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply alkali-resistant primer by airless spray on non-vented bare FC soffit overhead. ~18 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in. NON-VENTED ONLY. Bare FC absorbs heavily — slower spray rate than factory-primed surfaces.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. Full coverage on high-absorption surface.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Inspect for thin spots on high-absorption areas.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In at Fascia/Frieze Junctions — Coat 1

QT2.notes: Clean enough line at junctions overhead. Quick overhead brush work.

QT3.notes: Straight, consistent cut-in line overhead. Careful brush control.

QT4.notes: Crisp, precise cut-in at 3 ft viewing standard overhead. Slower, deliberate brush strokes.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush cut-in at fascia-soffit and frieze-soffit junctions overhead. Rate per SF of soffit (proxy for perimeter junction length). Overhead penalty baked into rates. Required for both brush/roll and spray methods. QT-scaled because precision increases significantly at higher tiers.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Straight, consistent cut-in line.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Crisp, precise cut-in line at 3 ft viewing standard.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush/Roll Overhead
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roller with extension pole for open field, brush for T&G grooves and edge detail overhead. ~30 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 150-200 SF/hr, overhead: 100-150 SF/hr). Thin coats required overhead to prevent sag. Back-brush after rolling to catch drips. Default method for ALL vented soffits.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage overhead. No drips or sags.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Consistent roller texture. Maintain wet edge overhead.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform appearance. No visible roller marks at 6 ft. T&G grooves fully coated.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray Overhead (Non-Vented Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray finish coat overhead on non-vented solid panel soffit. ~14 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 300-450 SF/hr, overhead: 200-300 SF/hr). NON-VENTED ONLY (FM-001). Lower pressure and tight fan pattern (413-515 tip) for controlled overhead application.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No drips or holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build overhead. No visible spray pattern at 6 ft.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: T&G Groove Brush-Back After Spray — Coat 1
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush paint into T&G groove joints overhead while spray coat is wet. ~24 sec per SF. Two-person operation: sprayer leads, brusher follows within 30-60 seconds. Spray alone does not penetrate T&G groove channels. Overhead brush-back is slow due to groove detail work at overhead angle. Rate is for the brusher only (sprayer separately timed in spray task).

defect_tolerance.QT3: All groove joints coated. Follow sprayer within 30-60 sec.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All groove channels fully coated. No dry spots. Consistent coverage.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Inspection — Overhead

QT3.notes: Quick scan from ladder for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays, drips. Overhead inspection needs headlamp.

QT4.notes: Systematic inspection with raking light overhead. Mark all visible defects. Check T&G grooves.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection of first finish coat from ladder/scaffold overhead. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: QT3 1500, QT4 800 SF/hr). Overhead inspection is slower because viewing angle is awkward and lighting must be supplemented with headlamp/portable light.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Quick scan. Note obvious runs, sags, holidays, drip marks.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic scan with raking light. All visible defects marked.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Light Sand — QT4 Only
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 220 grit light scuff between finish coats overhead. ~20 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 250-300 SF/hr, overhead: 150-200 SF/hr). QT4 only. Overhead sanding is slow and fatiguing — dust falls onto painter. PPE mandatory.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Light uniform scuff overhead. Remove nibs, drip marks, defects. No deep scratches.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Touch-Up

QT3.notes: Fix obvious defects overhead — minimal touch-up.

QT4.notes: Fix all found defects overhead. Blend repairs.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during interstage inspection overhead. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: QT3 2000, QT4 1000 SF/hr). Overhead touch-up is slower due to brush control at awkward angles.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects repaired. No visible runs or holidays remain.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired and blended. Repairs invisible at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth dust removal after intercoat sanding overhead. ~9 sec per SF. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: 500-600 SF/hr, overhead: 300-500 SF/hr). QT4 only (paired with TSK_SFIT_SAND_INTERCOAT).

defect_tolerance.QT4: All sanding dust removed. Surface clean for second finish coat.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In at Fascia/Frieze Junctions — Coat 2

QT3.notes: Straight, consistent cut-in line overhead. Final coat.

QT4.notes: Crisp, precise cut-in at 3 ft viewing standard overhead. Final appearance coat.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush cut-in at fascia-soffit and frieze-soffit junctions for second coat overhead. Same overhead-adjusted rates as coat 1 per tier. Final appearance coat — precision matters.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Straight, consistent cut-in line. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Crisp, precise cut-in line at 3 ft viewing standard. Final appearance coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush/Roll Overhead
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 brush/roll overhead. Primed and first-coated surface provides consistent absorption. Final appearance coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance. Maintain wet edge overhead.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform appearance. No visible roller marks at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray Overhead (Non-Vented Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 spray overhead. Consistent surface from first coat. NON-VENTED ONLY. Final appearance coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

task_production_rates.name: T&G Groove Brush-Back After Spray — Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 T&G brush-back. Final coat — all grooves must have full coverage.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All groove joints coated. Follow sprayer within 30-60 sec. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All groove channels fully coated. No missed grooves. Final appearance.

task_production_rates.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection — Overhead

QT2.notes: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for misses and drip marks.

QT3.notes: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft. Check all elevations. Verify T&G groove coverage.

QT4.notes: Ground-level + ladder. Binoculars for upper soffits. 6 ft viewing standard. Raking light on primary elevations.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final walkthrough of completed soffit from ground level and ladder. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: QT2 2000, QT3 1200, QT4 500 SF/hr). Soffit inspection is harder — must look UP instead of straight ahead. Drip marks and sag are the primary defect patterns to check.

defect_tolerance.QT2: No obvious misses or drip marks visible from ground.
defect_tolerance.QT3: No defects visible at 6-10 ft from ground level. T&G grooves covered.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No defects visible at 6 ft with binoculars. Coverage uniform. Edge lines crisp.

task_production_rates.name: Final Touch-Up — Overhead

QT2.notes: Fix obvious misses and drip marks overhead.

QT4.notes: Fix every defect overhead. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection overhead from ladder/scaffold. Overhead penalty baked in (vertical baseline: QT2 3000, QT3 1500, QT4 600 SF/hr). Overhead touch-up is precise brush work at awkward angle.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Obvious misses and drip marks touched up.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All noted defects repaired.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended seamlessly.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Material Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all landscape tarps, hardscape drop cloths, fascia masking tape/film, fixture bags. ~10 sec per SF of protected area. Faster than setup — pull and fold vs. stake and secure. Ground-level task (no overhead penalty for removing ground-level protection).

defect_tolerance.QT3: All materials removed. No tape residue on fascia. Check landscape for drip damage.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All materials removed. Check for tape residue. Inspect protected surfaces for paint transfer.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Equipment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean rollers, brushes, extension poles. Flush airless sprayer if used (non-vented soffit). Clean tips and filters. ~30 min per session. Same as siding sibling — equipment cleaning is ground-level work.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full flush. Tips and filters cleaned. Extension poles cleaned.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full flush cycle. Tips and filters cleaned and inspected. Equipment ready for next use.

task_production_rates.name: Site Debris Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Collect debris — sandpaper, caulk tubes, tape, sealer containers, paint cans, roller covers, plastic sheeting. Final site walkthrough. ~20 min. Same as siding sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials removed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Site restored. Walkthrough with customer. No evidence of work activity.

factor_modifiers.name: Access Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Access type drives production rate reduction for elevated work. Applied per elevation on top of overhead-adjusted base rates.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied per elevation. Ground tasks (landscape/hardscape protect setup/teardown, fixture masking, equipment setup, cleanup) are ground-level and not affected. Base rates already include overhead penalty — FAC_EXT_ACCESS stacks on top for elevated soffit access.

factor_modifiers.name: Vented Soffit Application Penalty
factor_modifiers.description: Vented soffit requires careful brush/roll technique to avoid driving paint into vent perforations. Slight slowdown on finish application tasks.
factor_modifiers.notes: Only applies to brush/roll tasks — spray is PROHIBITED on vented soffit (FM-001). Painters must slow down near vent perforations to avoid forcing paint into attic space. 15% time increase on vented panels.

factor_modifiers.name: Tongue-and-Groove Joint Complexity Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: T&G board soffit has many joints requiring brush attention to work paint into grooves. Applies to brush/roll application tasks.
factor_modifiers.notes: 20% time increase for T&G board soffit. Grooves require brush-in technique on each joint. Solid panel (plywood, fiber cement, vinyl) has smooth surface — no joint penalty. T&G brush-back tasks (TSK_SFIT_TG_BRUSH_BACK_1/2) already reflect groove work in their base rate — do NOT apply this modifier to those tasks.

factor_modifiers.name: Quality Tier Production Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier affects pace and scrutiny on tasks with qt_scaled classification. Binary tasks are not affected — they execute the same regardless of tier.
factor_modifiers.applies_to: qt_scaled tasks only (TSK_SFIT_CUTIN_FASCIA_1, TSK_SFIT_CUTIN_FASCIA_2, TSK_SFIT_INSPECT_COAT, TSK_SFIT_TOUCHUP_REPAIR, TSK_SFIT_FINAL_INSPECT, TSK_SFIT_FINAL_TOUCHUP)
factor_modifiers.formula: Qt_scaled tasks use qt_rates directly. This modifier applies to binary tasks that have tier-sensitive pace.
factor_modifiers.notes: QT2 is faster (less scrutiny). QT4 is slower (more scrutiny). Qt_scaled tasks already have per-tier rates — FAC_QT is informational for those. For binary tasks, FAC_QT may be applied by the engine for global pace adjustment.

factor_modifiers.name: Exterior Substrate Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Substrate condition affects prep task rates. New construction soffit is typically in good condition.
factor_modifiers.notes: NC soffit is typically new_clean or light_construction_debris. Heavy debris (drywall dust accumulation, grout residue from overhead tile work) is possible but uncommon.

factor_modifiers.name: Wind Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Wind blocks spray application and slows brush/roll work on elevated soffit. High wind forces spray to brush/roll fallback.
factor_modifiers.formula: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. High wind: spray tasks excluded, switch to brush/roll.
factor_modifiers.notes: Soffit is partially sheltered by the roof overhang — less wind exposure than siding. But elevated soffit on ladder/scaffold is still vulnerable. Moderate wind slows brush/roll 15%. High wind stops spray entirely — SOP exclude_when rule.

factor_modifiers.name: Sun Exposure Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Soffits are sheltered from direct sun by the roof overhang. Minimal sun exposure impact on most soffits.
factor_modifiers.notes: Soffit is typically in shade (under roof overhang). Full sun exposure is rare — only on very wide overhangs or south-facing with low angle. Minimal impact vs siding sun exposure modifier.

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Temperature Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Extreme surface temperatures affect recoat intervals. Soffit is generally cooler than siding (shaded).
factor_modifiers.notes: Soffit surfaces stay cooler than siding (shaded). Cold weather is more relevant — extends recoat intervals, reduces daily productive hours. Hot weather minimal impact on shaded soffit.

quality_effects.notes: Economy tier. Single finish coat on primed surface. No interstage module. Minimal inspection. Acceptable for sheltered soffit where visibility is low (high overhang, dark color).
Standard tier. Two finish coats. Interstage inspection but no sanding. Full edge seal, cut-in at junctions. Standard residential soffit quality.
Premium tier. Two finish coats. Light sand between coats (220 grit overhead). Systematic inspection with raking light. Premium materials. For high-visibility soffits on wide overhangs.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Solid panel soffit, non-vented, ground access — baseline brush/roll
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Best case brush/roll — solid panel, non-vented, ground. 120 SF/hr overhead (already reduced from 150-200 vertical).

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: T&G board soffit, vented, ladder access — common residential brush/roll
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Common residential scenario. ~64 SF/hr brush/roll on vented T&G soffit from ladder. Slow but expected for overhead T&G detail work.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: T&G board soffit, vented, scaffold access — worst case brush/roll
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Near worst case brush/roll. ~54 SF/hr. Under 4.0x stacking cap. Very slow but expected for overhead vented T&G from scaffold.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Solid panel soffit, non-vented, ground access — spray baseline
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Best case spray — solid panel, non-vented, ground. 250 SF/hr overhead spray.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Solid panel soffit, non-vented, scaffold access — spray elevated
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Spray from scaffold on non-vented soffit. ~156 SF/hr. Comfortable within 4.0x cap.

overhead_rate_design_notes.rationale: All base rates in this spec already reflect the overhead work penalty (~25-35% reduction from vertical siding baselines). The FAC_SFIT_OVERHEAD modifier from research (1.35) is NOT applied as a separate stacking modifier because that would double-count the overhead penalty. Instead, overhead is pre-baked into every rate.

vertical_to_overhead_reductions.inspection: Vertical QT3 1500 → Overhead 1000, Vertical QT4 800 → Overhead 500 (~33% reduction)
vertical_to_overhead_reductions.touch_up: Vertical QT3 2000 → Overhead 1500, Vertical QT4 1000 → Overhead 700 (~25-30% reduction)

overhead_rate_design_notes.stacking_with_access: FAC_EXT_ACCESS stacks on top of overhead-adjusted base rates. Example: ladder access (1.35) on overhead brush/roll (120 SF/hr) = 89 SF/hr effective. This represents BOTH the overhead penalty AND the ladder access penalty.

assumptions: Base rates include overhead work penalty (~25-35% reduction from vertical baselines). Do NOT apply FAC_SFIT_OVERHEAD as a separate stacking modifier.
FAC_EXT_ACCESS, FAC_SFIT_VENT_COMPLEXITY, and FAC_SFIT_TG_JOINTS stack multiplicatively on top of overhead-adjusted base rates.
Modifier stacking cap: 4.0x maximum combined. Worst case in this spec: vented + T&G + scaffold = 2.208x (well under cap).
Spray application is eligible ONLY for non-vented solid panel soffit. Vented soffit: brush/roll only (FM-001).
T&G groove brush-back tasks (TSK_SFIT_TG_BRUSH_BACK_1/2) already reflect groove work in their base rate — FAC_SFIT_TG_JOINTS does NOT apply to those tasks.
Cut-in tasks (TSK_SFIT_CUTIN_FASCIA_1/2) use SF as proxy for perimeter junction length. Rate is per SF of soffit area.
Protection setup/teardown, equipment setup, and cleanup are ground-level tasks — no overhead penalty applied.
Spot-prime knots and seal cut edges are EA-based manual capture tasks — estimator enters count.
Environmental modifiers (wind, sun, temperature) are declared per exterior spec policy but have minimal impact on soffit (sheltered by roof overhang).
crew_size = 1 for all tasks except T&G brush-back on spray (requires sprayer + brusher, but rate is per brusher only).
risks: Overhead work fatigue may reduce actual production rates below estimates — especially on long runs of T&G soffit from ladder. Flag for field calibration.
Vented soffit + T&G + scaffold (worst case 2.208x) is slow production (~54 SF/hr brush/roll) but well within 4.0x stacking cap.
Spot-prime knot count and seal cut edge count are manual capture — estimator must inspect soffit to determine counts. Under-count risks tannin bleed (knots) or moisture wicking (cut edges).
Caulk rate (55 LF/hr overhead) is an estimate — overhead caulking is substantially slower than vertical due to gravity pulling caulk from the bead. Flag for field calibration.
Spray rates on non-vented soffit (250 SF/hr) are derived from vertical spray rates with overhead reduction. Limited field data for overhead spray — flag for calibration.
Vinyl soffit bonding primer must be topcoated within 1 week (RISK-SFIT-008). Production scheduling constraint — not a rate modifier but affects project planning.
Fascia masking task assumes fascia is already finished. In top-down NC sequence, this task is typically skipped.
validation_plan: Time 3 brush/roll finish projects on smooth solid panel soffit at ground/ladder access to calibrate baseline 120 SF/hr.
Time 2 T&G board soffit projects (vented, brush/roll) to validate 1.20x T&G joint modifier.
Time 1 spray finish project on non-vented solid panel soffit to validate 250 SF/hr overhead spray rate.
Compare overhead caulk rates (55 LF/hr) against vertical caulk rates (90 LF/hr siding sibling) on same project.
Track spot-prime knot counts per project to develop estimating heuristic (knots per 8 ft board on cedar T&G).
Track seal cut edge counts per project for HardieSoffit panel layouts.
Compare fixture masking time (overhead, 10 EA/hr) vs siding fixture masking (wall-mounted, 15 EA/hr).
Verify vented soffit 1.15x penalty by timing brush/roll on same project with mixed vented/non-vented sections.
